title: Self-Creating Toolkit Demo
description: Demonstrates code_toolkit: an agent writes a text_stats_toolkit module at runtime, then the workflow immediately hot-imports and calls it to analyse user-supplied text.

args.name: text_stats_toolkit
args.code:
# text_stats_toolkit - auto-generated by code_toolkit_demo workflow

class TextStatsToolkit:
    """Text statistics tools: word count, keyword extraction, and summarisation."""
    __toolkit__ = True

    def word_count(self, text: str) -> dict:
        """Count words, sentences, and characters in text.
        Returns a dict with keys: words, sentences, chars, avg_word_len."""
        import re
        words = text.split()
        sentences = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r'[.!?]+', text) if s.strip()]
        return {
            "words":        len(words),
            "sentences":    len(sentences),
            "chars":        len(text),
            "avg_word_len": round(sum(len(w) for w in words) / max(len(words), 1), 1),
        }

    def extract_keywords(self, text: str, top_n: int = 5) -> list:
        """Extract the most frequent meaningful words from text.
        top_n: number of keywords to return (default 5)."""
        import re
        STOP = {
            "the","a","an","is","are","was","were","be","been","have","has",
            "had","do","does","did","will","would","could","should","may",
            "might","must","can","it","its","this","that","and","but","or",
            "nor","for","in","of","on","to","at","by","from","with","not",
            "no","as","if","so","then","than","also","into","over","after",
        }
        words = re.findall(r"[a-z']+", text.lower())
        words = [w for w in words if w not in STOP and len(w) > 3]
        counts = {}
        for w in words:
            counts[w] = counts.get(w, 0) + 1
        return sorted(counts, key=lambda k: counts[k], reverse=True)[:top_n]

    def summarize(self, text: str) -> str:
        """Return the first sentence as a quick extractive summary."""
        import re
        sentences = re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', text.strip())
        return sentences[0] if sentences else text[:200]

nodes.query: Toolkit created! Now enter some text to analyse:

nodes.script:
# Hot-import the toolkit that was just written to disk by create_toolkit.
# We use importlib so this works even in the same workflow run.
import importlib, sys

mod_name = 'contrib.toolkits.text_stats_toolkit'
if mod_name in sys.modules:
    del sys.modules[mod_name]          # force fresh load
mod = importlib.import_module(mod_name)
tk  = mod.TextStatsToolkit()

text     = str(input)
stats    = tk.word_count(text)
keywords = tk.extract_keywords(text, top_n=7)
summary  = tk.summarize(text)

lines = [
    f'Words:        {stats["words"]}',
    f'Sentences:    {stats["sentences"]}',
    f'Characters:   {stats["chars"]}',
    f'Avg word len: {stats["avg_word_len"]}',
    f'Keywords:     {", ".join(keywords)}',
    f'Summary:      {summary}',
]
output = '\n'.join(lines)
